Industry whitepaper.redistribution: quote fragments with attribution and a link to the original

IACR ePrint.terms: IACR ePrint: authors retain copyright; acquisition may include an abstract or PDF text. Check the linked paper for reuse terms.

arXiv.terms: Licence is set per paper by its authors (CC-BY, CC-BY-NC-SA, or arXiv's non-exclusive licence). Check the abs page before reusing a text beyond quotation.
arXiv.redistribution: quote fragments with attribution; check the paper for reuse

OpenAlex work.terms: Work discovered through OpenAlex; acquisition may be abstract-only. Licence is set per work; check the linked source before reuse.
OpenAlex work.redistribution: quote fragments with attribution; check the source licence

HAL Open Science.terms: HAL repository: licence is document-specific; check the linked deposit.
HAL Open Science.redistribution: quote briefly with attribution; check the deposit licence

We show how to compute exact attention with fewer HBM reads/writes and without storing large intermediate matrices for the backward pass.
This yields an attention algorithm that is both memory efficient and faster
in wall-clock time.
We analyze its IO complexity, showing that our method requires
much fewer HBM accesses compared to standard attention.
We further show that can serve as a useful primitive by extending it to handle block-sparse attention.

We introduce the Episodic Memory with Questions and Feedback task (EM-QnF). 
Unlike EM-NLQ, which answers a natural language query in a one-shot manner, EM-QnF extends the task by allowing users to provide natural language feedback that guides the model toward a more accurate prediction.
